### Factual Comparison by Category

#### 1. Defense
* **LeBron James:** Accumulated five NBA All-Defensive First Team selections (2008–09 through 2012–13) and one All-Defensive Second Team selection (2013–14) [lebron_accolades_320].
* **Michael Jordan:** Specific defensive metrics and defensive accolades for Jordan are not present in the provided evidence. 
* *Tradeoff:* While LeBron's resume demonstrates sustained peak defensive recognition (six combined All-Defensive selections) [lebron_accolades_320], a direct factual comparison is constrained because Jordan’s defensive honors are missing from the data.

---

#### 2. Scoring
* **LeBron James:** Ranks #1 on the NBA all-time regular season scoring list with 38,390 points across 1,410 games and 53,741 minutes on 50.5% field goal shooting [lebron_scoring_640]. He has one scoring title (2007–08) [lebron_accolades_320] and recorded one of the 11 individual seasons in NBA history averaging over 30 points per 75 possessions at +6% relative true shooting (rTS) [jordan_defense_2720].
* **Michael Jordan:** Ranks #5 all-time with 32,292 regular season points [lebron_scoring_720]. Jordan owns four of the 11 seasons in league history featuring 30+ points per 75 possessions at +6% rTS [jordan_defense_2720]. His scoring profile maintained high volume and shot creation in the postseason with virtually no loss in efficiency [jordan_defense_2720].
* *Tradeoff:* LeBron holds the cumulative scoring advantage, leading all players in total career points [lebron_scoring_640]. Jordan holds the high-efficiency peak scoring advantage, producing four separate high-volume, highly efficient 30+ pt/75 seasons compared to LeBron's one [jordan_defense_2720].

---

#### 3. Accolades
* **LeBron James:**
  * 4 Regular Season MVPs (2008–09, 2009–10, 2011–12, 2012–13) [lebron_accolades_160].
  * 13 All-NBA First Team selections [lebron_accolades_160].
  * 4 All-NBA Second Team selections [lebron_accolades_160].
  * 6 All-Defensive selections (5 First Team, 1 Second Team) [lebron_accolades_320].
  * 2003–04 Rookie of the Year [lebron_accolades_320].
  * 1 Scoring title and 1 Assists title [lebron_accolades_320].
* **Michael Jordan:** Specific accolade counts (MVPs, All-NBA selections, Finals MVPs, or championships) are not provided in the evidence.
* *Tradeoff:* LeBron’s documented accolades reflect extraordinary consistency at the highest tier of the league over multiple decades [lebron_accolades_160]. Jordan’s formal accolade totals cannot be fully compared using only the provided text.

---

#### 4. Longevity
* **LeBron James:** Maintained top-tier play across at least 1,410 games and 53,741 minutes [lebron_scoring_640], securing First Team All-NBA nods from 2005–06 through 2019–20 [lebron_accolades_160].
* **Michael Jordan:** Experienced two career interruptions, including a baseball sabbatical in 1993–1995 [jordan_defense_3120] and a three-year layoff before playing with the Washington Wizards [jordan_longevity_320]. In Washington, his effectiveness was curtailed by age and injuries [jordan_longevity_320], though the team improved from 19–63 prior to his arrival to competing near playoff contention [jordan_longevity_880].
* *Tradeoff:* LeBron demonstrates continuous, unbroken longevity at an elite level [lebron_scoring_640, lebron_accolades_160]. Jordan's longevity includes multi-year absences and a final stint where injuries and age visibly limited his capabilities [jordan_longevity_320].

---

#### 5. Playoffs
* **Michael Jordan:** Logged 179 career playoff games [jordan_playoffs_2560]. Specific playoff scoring marks in the records include 36.7 points per game over 16 games in 1990 [jordan_playoffs_2160] and 32.4 points per game across 21 games in 1998 [jordan_playoffs_2560]. Jordan's postseason volume and creation sustained Chicago’s offense without dropping in efficiency [jordan_defense_2720].
* **LeBron James:** Playoff games, scoring, and efficiency metrics are omitted from the supplied records.
* *Tradeoff:* Jordan exhibits documented high-scoring postseason campaigns maintaining elevated efficiency [jordan_defense_2720, jordan_playoffs_2560]; the available texts do not supply LeBron's playoff statistics to allow a head-to-head evaluation.

---

### Separation of Factual Evidence vs. Subjective GOAT Judgments

* **Factual Evidence:** Concrete recorded facts include LeBron's all-time scoring lead (38,390 points) [lebron_scoring_640], his 4 MVPs and 13 First Team All-NBA selections [lebron_accolades_160], Jordan’s 4 seasons of 30+ points per 75 possessions at +6% rTS [jordan_defense_2720], Jordan's 179 playoff games [jordan_playoffs_2560], and Washington’s records before, during, and after Jordan [jordan_longevity_880].
* **Subjective Judgments:** Determining the "Greatest of All Time" depends on subjective weighting:
  * Proponents of Jordan view his ability to lift slightly above-average team offenses by 5 to 6 points as "GOAT-worthy" peak impact [jordan_defense_3120], often choosing to discount or ignore his Washington years when judging his prime legacy [jordan_longevity_320].
  * Proponents of LeBron prioritize historic cumulative durability, unparalleled career scoring totals [lebron_scoring_640], and elite accolades sustained over nearly two decades [lebron_accolades_160].
